You are a fix worker on the loop-factory repo. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory — edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit, branch, or push; leave changes uncommitted. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. No network access. Python stdlib + PyYAML only.

CONTEXT: an adversarial pre-merge review found integrity defects in the podcast watchdog's incident/records layer. Charter rules that govern the fixes: one incident = one thread forever; NEVER suppress or downgrade a RED signal; a resolved fingerprint recurring is a department_defect that MUST re-escalate; records are single-writer with strictly increasing epochs; missing evidence is never healthy.

OWNERSHIP: you own ONLY: departments/podcast/runtime/fingerprint_dedup.py, departments/podcast/runtime/escalate_outbox.py, departments/podcast/runtime/record.py, departments/podcast/tests/test_watchdog_spine.py, departments/podcast/tests/test_records_integrity.py (new file). Never modify anything else (sense/compare/sensors/heal files are frozen — recent concurrent rounds own them).

FINDINGS TO FIX:
1. HIGH fingerprint_dedup.py ~:255 — merging a newer LOWER-severity candidate into an open incident overwrites the higher severity (a failed probe followed by a degraded unknown probe downgrades HIGH to MED). Fix: while an incident is open (or department_defect), merged severity = max by rank (critical>high>med>low); failure_class may track the newest candidate but severity never decreases until the incident is resolved.
2. HIGH fingerprint_dedup.py ~:324 — a MISSING candidates file (as opposed to a present-but-empty one) defaults to an empty list, letting the auto-resolve healthy-cycle counter advance from historical observations, so lost comparison output can resolve an open incident. Fix: distinguish the two — missing/unreadable candidates input = evidence-unavailable cycle: no healthy accrual for ANY incident, no state transitions, and emit a clear stderr/receipt note; present-and-empty = genuinely zero candidates, healthy accrual allowed.
3. HIGH escalate_outbox.py ~:48 — incidents transitioned to department_defect keep their escalated=True flag from the earlier open phase, so a resolved fingerprint recurring NEVER produces the required root-cause escalation. Fix: the transition into department_defect (recurrence) must produce exactly ONE new escalation (track a per-state escalation marker, e.g. escalated_defect, so re-runs stay exactly-once).
4. HIGH escalate_outbox.py ~:53 — outbox append and the incidents.json escalated-state update are neither atomic nor locked: a crash between them (or a concurrent runner) emits duplicate escalation rows on retry. Fix: take an exclusive fcntl.flock on a <state-dir>/.records.lock file around the read-decide-append-update sequence; if the outbox append succeeds but the state write fails, the next run must detect the already-appended row (dedupe by fingerprint+state marker in the outbox read-back) instead of appending again.
5. HIGH record.py ~:86 — epoch fencing is an unlocked read-check-replace: two writers can read the same epoch and both write. Fix: hold the SAME <state-dir>/.records.lock flock across the entire runs-append → STATE replace → heartbeat sequence so the fence is race-free; a lock acquisition timeout (a few seconds) = fail loudly, never proceed unlocked.
6. MED — strengthen negative coverage using the existing poisoned fixture departments/podcast/tests/fixtures/poisoned/resolved_fingerprint_recurs.json: feed it through the real dedup + escalate path and prove the department_defect transition AND its new escalation row.

TESTS: put new tests in departments/podcast/tests/test_records_integrity.py; update test_watchdog_spine.py ONLY where existing assertions encode the old behavior (list every changed assertion in fix-summary). Required: severity never downgrades while open; missing-candidates cycle freezes auto-resolve (and a subsequent present-empty cycle resumes it); defect recurrence escalates exactly once across two consecutive runs; concurrent-writer simulation (two sequential writers with interleaved reads, or flock contention via a held lock in a thread) proves single-writer fencing; crash-between-append-and-update simulation proves no duplicate outbox row on rerun. ALL existing tests must pass.

HOW TO RUN: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest departments/podcast/tests/ -q

OUTPUT CONTRACT: leave changes uncommitted; write ./fix-summary.md ('# Fix Summary', '## Summary', '## Files Changed', '## Verification', '## Assumptions', <700 words) mapping each finding to fix + test.
